low_pressure_flushing.secondary_impacts: Can drive oil into sediment if misapplied; mobilised oil must be recovered

low_pressure_heated_flushing.secondary_impacts: Heat harms sensitive biota; excluded on wetlands

high_pressure_washing.secondary_impacts: High disturbance; drives oil down if used on soft substrate

high_pressure_heated_washing.secondary_impacts: Hot-water washing initially worsened recovery at Exxon Valdez sites (NOAA OR&R)

surface_washing_agents.secondary_impacts: Chemical residue and mobilised-oil recovery concerns

solidifiers.secondary_impacts: Added material and waste; limited field evidence

mechanical_removal.secondary_impacts: Sediment loss and habitat damage; excluded on marsh and mudflat

sediment_relocation.secondary_impacts: Redistributes oil; only on exposed beaches

sediment_mixing.secondary_impacts: Can bury or spread oil; not for soft or sensitive habitat

bioremediation.secondary_impacts: Effectiveness depends on nutrients, oxygen and access; limited bioaugmentation evidence (NOAA)

vegetation_cutting.secondary_impacts: Removes biomass and can increase erosion; only where sensitivity is high

inputs.class_rules: E excluded > A benefit > D harm under conditions > B no clear evidence; C natural recovery
inputs.ordering: within a class: lower bound of the 90% benefit interval where it exists (edge loss avoided by year 8 in m, then vegetation cover ratio at year 2, then literature lnRR lower bound; units are never mixed), then the ASSUMED ecological score (higher = lower disturbance first), then name

habitat_descriptors.asphalt_pavement_risk: yes: chronic sheening and asphalt pavements are likely along sheltered portions where accumulations are heavy

literature_notes.statement: High-pressure hot-water washing (Exxon Valdez, Prince William Sound): hardshell clam (littleneck) abundance at washed sites was 92-97% below oiled, unwashed sites at 1, 2, 3 and 5 years after treatment (rows B018-B021, grade B, observational, treatment chosen by responders; B019 n = 3 vs 4 stations). Macroinfauna abundance and richness were also lower (B014-B016).
literature_notes.label: literature, not a prediction
literature_notes.source: literature_effects.csv B014-B022; Houghton JP et al. (1996) NOAA Tech. Memo. NOS ORCA 91 (docs/reference/literature/Houghton_1996_PWS_Biology_ORCA91.pdf, opened this session); tables 4-6 to 4-9 exist in the report

literature_notes.statement: Littleneck clams at hot-water-washed sites needed until 2000 (11 years after the spill) to converge with unoiled sites, because washing winnowed fine sediment (row B024; abstract-only extraction, recovery-time ratio 3.67, no variance).

literature_notes.statement: Exxon Valdez oil persists in the subsurface of Prince William Sound gravel beaches: field data and modelling indicate some oil was trapped in the anoxic lower layers of a two-layer beach when the water table was low; remediation was stopped in 1992 on the assumption of fast natural loss.
